title: How to Work with AI Coding Agents: Spec-Driven Development, Context and Loop Engineering, Workflows
summary: Live workshop: spec before code, AGENTS.md context, groomed tasks with acceptance criteria, goal loops and PM/engineer/QA subagent graph.

assertions.quote: ask me one question at a time ... we are moving towards something that we decide not the agent decides

verdicts.note: Requirements clarification before implementation is well-established practice and widely reported to reduce agent rework.

assertions.quote: the agent has to make a lot of assumptions ... That's why we want to first build the specification

verdicts.note: Clear requirements, examples and references reliably improve agent output; the caveat is that bloated context can hurt, so curation matters.

assertions.quote: for the agent not to think about these things all the time ... creating this file called uh agents.mmd

verdicts.note: Persistent instruction files measurably steer agent behavior; overlong or contradictory ones reduce adherence.

assertions.quote: for each new task I try to start a session a new session

verdicts.note: Fresh context avoids accumulated noise, but compaction is useful when state is hard to reconstruct; it is a tradeoff, not a rule.

assertions.quote: I want to make it as unambiguous as possible ... the agent doesn't need to make any decisions

verdicts.note: Checkable acceptance criteria give agents a stopping condition and give reviewers a test; out-of-scope lists reduce scope creep. Standard practice that carries over well to agents.

assertions.quote: The tester often finds some things that a software engineer missed

verdicts.note: Fresh-context reviewers avoid self-confirmation and context bloat; plausible and commonly practiced but little hard evidence.

assertions.quote: your token consumption goes like I don't know four five times more ... what you get in return is uh better quality

verdicts.note: Separate reviewer/QA passes do catch more defects and clearly multiply token cost; evidence that full role pipelines beat a single well-prompted agent is mixed.

assertions.quote: I will not need to babysit this agent

verdicts.note: Goal/loop features keep agents going through backlogs, but unattended runs drift or game checks without good verification; works when acceptance tests are strong.

assertions.quote: this thing kind of disynchronized from the codebase ... I can just actually delete it

verdicts.note: Agents treat repo docs as authoritative; outdated docs demonstrably steer them wrong.

assertions.quote: you get more uh for the same plan in Codex. So you get higher limits

verdicts.note: Rate-limit and cost complaints about Claude Code are common and real for heavy users, but competitors also cap usage; anecdotal, from a competitor's video.

assertions.quote: LLMs have this knowledge cutff ... it suggest to use GPT40

verdicts.note: Training cutoffs reliably cause stale version and model suggestions; checking against current docs is necessary.

assertions.quote: I run it on a remote machine that um if something happens to this machine it will not affect my computer

verdicts.note: Agents have deleted files and run destructive commands when unrestricted; vendors themselves recommend containers/VMs for skip-permissions modes.
